name: SparkFun Qwiic Twist
description: 24-detent rotary encoder with a built-in RGB LED and push switch, read over I2C: an ATtiny84 running SparkFun's firmware keeps a signed 16-bit detent count, the turn difference, pressed/clicked/moved status and time stamps, sets the knob colour (kept in EEPROM) and drives an open-drain INT line. 3.3 V board (no regulator) with 2.2 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups. I2C address 0x3F (0x3E with the ADR jumper closed; any 0x08-0x77 can be set in software). Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic Twist - RGB Rotary Encoder Breakout (DEV-15083), 6-pin 0.1" header GND, 3.3V, SDA, SCL, INT, RST plus two Qwiic connectors.
eli5: A knob you can turn and push, with a coloured light inside; a little chip counts the clicks as you turn it and tells your board over two wires.

pins.name: 3.3V
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V only (no regulator; the I2C and INT pull-ups go to this pin)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (2.2 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (2.2 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, active low, open drain with a 10 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V on the board (INT jumper); goes low on a button press/release or after the knob stops turning. Not needed for basic use

pins.name: RST
pins.description: ATtiny84 reset input, active low (holds the Twist in reset while low). Leave unconnected

supplierQuery: SparkFun Qwiic Twist RGB Rotary Encoder DEV-15083
buildNotes: Power it from 3.3 V only: there is no regulator and the 2.2 kOhm SDA/SCL pull-ups go to its 3.3V pin.
Register reads: write the register number, then read; 16-bit values are little-endian (low byte first). Register 0x00 reads 0x5C.
Count: register 0x05, 2 bytes, signed 16-bit, one count per detent (24 per turn), clockwise counts up.
Status register 0x01: bit 1 = knob pressed now, bit 2 = clicked (pressed and released), bit 0 = moved; write 0 to clear clicked and moved (pressed is read-only).
Knob colour: write red, green, blue (0-255) to registers 0x0D-0x0F in one write; the firmware stores them in EEPROM.
Default address 0x3F; closing the ADR jumper forces 0x3E. A new address (0x08-0x77) written to register 0x18 is kept in EEPROM.
INT (open drain, 10 kOhm pull-up) and RST are only for advanced use; leave them unconnected otherwise.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_twist import QwiicTwist

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
twist = QwiicTwist(i2c)
print('ID ok, firmware %d.%d' % twist.version())
while True:
    print('count=%d pressed=%d' % (twist.count(), 1 if twist.pressed() else 0))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
